role.altitude: The driver keeps driving, checking the van, delivering, taking payment and dealing with incidents; copying mileage, delivery sheets, timesheets and receipts onto paper shrinks.
skills_to_grow: Recording deliveries, hours and exceptions in the driver app as they happen
role.ambitious_version: A driver whose day ends at the last drop, not at a desk with paperwork.

tasks.short: Do the walk-around check, log mileage and fuel, record deliveries and exceptions, record hours and breaks, write billing statements for extra services, hand in paperwork, and have the office type it into the systems.

steps.what: Driver does the walk-around defect check and writes it in the vehicle log
Driver writes start and end mileage and fuel in the vehicle log
Driver records each delivery, signature, time and exception on the paper delivery sheet or consignment note
Driver records working hours and breaks: on a paper timesheet today; by tapping start, breaks and end in the app after the change, which adds up the totals
Driver checks the day's hours in the app: start, breaks and end match the shift worked
Driver releases the day's checked hours to payroll

Driver records extra services such as waiting time and extra stops: on paper billing statements today; after the change at the stop in the app, with customer, stop and times taken from the delivery record
Driver checks the day's extra services before release: each charge matches what happened at the stop, with its reason and time
Driver releases the checked extra services for invoicing
Driver hands in the paper records at the depot at day end
Planner types delivery records, extra services and hours into the transport system and for payroll

approvals.approved_version: The day's start, break and end times exactly as checked by the driver in s4c, released once from the app to payroll for that shift; any correction needs a new check and release.

The day's extra services with customer, reason and time exactly as checked by the driver in s5c, released once from the app to invoicing in the transport system; any change needs a new check and release.

tasks.design: A driver app linked to the transport system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) replaces the paper: the driver taps the walk-around checklist, scans each delivery and takes the signature on the phone, records exceptions and extra services at the stop, and taps start, breaks and end of shift. Mileage comes from the van's telematics unit and fuel from the fuel card transactions, so the vehicle log fills itself. Delivery records are saved in the transport system as the driver makes them. At the end of the shift the driver checks the day's hours and the extra services and releases each: hours to payroll, extra services for invoicing. Only paper consignment notes from foreign shippers are still handed in and typed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Without a driver app, every record was written on paper and typed again at the office.
tasks.enabler_now: Transport systems come with driver apps, electronic consignment notes and telematics links.
tasks.still_hard: Paper consignment notes still required abroad and from some shippers.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a fault on the van before it becomes a breakdown.
tasks.altitude: The driver's evening paperwork mostly goes; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: How much faster invoices go out when delivery records arrive the same day.

evidence.claim: Electronic consignment notes are created, issued and signed inside a transport system.
A Dutch carrier switched to a transport system with a driver app and now invoices in 1-2 days instead of up to a week (vendor case, no period).
From 1 July 2026, vans of 2.5 to 3.5 tonnes in paid international transport need a tachograph, which then records hours.
Telematics and driver apps observe location and behaviour and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the morning check to records in the transport system; invoicing and payroll runs are outside.

Input contract for s2: odometer readings from the telematics unit fitted in about 90% of vans, and refuelling from fuel card transactions sent by the card provider; the driver types mileage for vans without a unit and cash refuels; s2 is priced at that coverage.
Input contract for s3 to s5: the driver's own scans, signatures, taps and exception codes in the app at each stop; these are actual deliveries and times, not the planned stop list.
Coverage: about 85% of deliveries carry an electronic consignment note or scannable label; paper notes from foreign shippers are still handed in (s6) and typed (s7).
Hours are recorded by the driver's own taps; no idle-time or per-driver scores are made from the data.

Sizing: the walk-around check and its record keep their full time, because tapping a checklist takes as long as writing it. s3 keeps 65 because the scan replaces writing consignment numbers and times on 85% of deliveries while signatures and exceptions stay. s4 keeps 80 because each start, break and end is still recorded and only totals fall away. s5 keeps 50 because customer, stop and times come from the delivery record. Both checks and both releases keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether vans have telematics units and fuel cards.
Share of shipments with paper consignment notes.
research_questions: How many delivery records still need office correction?

already_counted.description: Driver corrects app records the transport system rejects.

incremental.description: Driver keeps the app updated and reports app faults.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older vans without telematics (s2 keeps 50) and many paper consignment notes from foreign shippers (s3 keeps 85, s6 keeps 60) (23.1); high: fitted vans and 85% of deliveries scanned as assumed (39.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect payment at delivery, write receipts, count the cash at day end, turn in receipts and money at the depot, and settle differences with the cashier.

steps.what: Driver collects cash or card payment at delivery

Driver writes a receipt for each payment in the receipt book today; after the change the app fills the receipt from the payment record and the driver writes one only when a customer insists on a handwritten one
Driver checks the receipt before it is issued: amount, order and customer match the payment taken
Driver issues the checked receipt to the customer by e-mail or the van printer
Driver counts the cash at day end and fills in the cash statement
Driver turns in receipts and money received from deliveries to the depot cashier
Depot cashier counts the money against the statement and books it
Driver settles differences with the cashier

approvals.approved_version: Each receipt with amount, order and customer exactly as checked by the driver in s2c, issued once to that customer by e-mail or the van printer; a corrected receipt needs a new check.

tasks.design: The driver app takes card payments through a connected card reader and records cash payments the driver taps in, and it fills the receipt from that payment record; the driver checks it and issues it by e-mail or the van printer. At day end the app shows the expected cash from the driver's own cash entries; the driver counts the actual cash and enters the count, and the cashier sees expected and counted amounts. Handing in the money and settling differences stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Payments were recorded only in a receipt book, so expected cash had to be added up by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Driver apps link card readers and record cash taken per delivery.
tasks.still_hard: Customers who pay cash and dispute amounts.
tasks.human_edge: Settling a cash difference on the doorstep without losing the customer.
tasks.altitude: Less writing and adding up; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether differences fall when expected cash comes from the app.

evidence.claim: Driver apps connect card readers and record cash taken per delivery.
Cash records per driver can monitor behaviour; using them to score drivers needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from taking payment to differences settled; banking the cash is outside.

Input contract for s2 and s3: payment records produced by the driver in s1, card payments by the connected reader and cash payments by the driver's tap; the expected cash is computed from them; the counted cash is the driver's actual count, not the expected amount.
Coverage: about 60% of payments by card after the reader is fitted; the s3 count still covers all cash.
Handing in money and settling differences keep their full time; the cashier's time is outside the driver's savings.
s2 keeps 10 for handwritten receipts some customers insist on; checking and issuing each receipt keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of deliveries paid on delivery.

already_counted.description: Driver taps each cash payment into the app at the door.

incremental.description: Driver charges and pairs the card reader.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most customers pay cash and want paper receipts, so s2 keeps 60 and the count shrinks little (s3 keeps 85) (12.6); high: about 60% of payments by card as assumed (26.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Report delays to base, report accidents and damage by phone and on the accident form, warn other drivers, and have the planner log the incident.

steps.what: Driver phones the base to report delays and the expected arrival time
Driver reports accidents and damage to base by telephone
Driver fills in the damage report: on the paper accident form today; in the app after the change, with location, time and van filled in
Driver takes photos of the damage
Driver checks the damage report and photos before sending: what happened is described as seen, the photos show the damage, and no bystanders' faces are in them
Driver sends the checked damage report with photos to the planner's incident log
Driver warns other vehicles about road situations by radio or group chat
Planner logs delays and incidents in the transport system

approvals.approved_version: The damage report with its photos and location exactly as checked by the driver in s3c, sent once to the planner's incident log in the transport system; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: The driver app sends the van's position to the transport system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), which shows the planner a live arrival estimate per stop, so routine traffic delays need no call; when stopped, the driver taps a delay reason for anything unusual. Accidents are still phoned in, and the driver fills in the damage report in the app with location and time filled in, takes photos, checks both and sends them to the planner's incident log; warning other drivers stays a radio or chat job. The app is used only when the van is stationary.
tasks.previous_blocker: The base knew about a delay only when the driver called.
tasks.enabler_now: Driver apps share position and arrival estimates with the transport system.
tasks.still_hard: Accidents and dangerous situations need a voice call.
tasks.human_edge: Judging when a situation is serious enough to stop and call.
tasks.altitude: Fewer routine calls; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether live estimates let customers be told before they call.

evidence.claim: Transport systems show live arrival estimates from driver app positions.
Tracking location observes drivers and needs works council consent; position data must not become per-driver idle scores.
A regulator fined a logistics firm EUR 32 million for scanner indicators of exact idle time and long retention.

assumptions: Boundary: from a delay or incident on the road to the incident log; claims handling is outside.
Input contract for s1: van position from the driver app, produced while the driver is logged in for the shift, used only for arrival estimates; fallback is a call.
Coverage: about 70% of delay reports are routine traffic delays the estimate shows; s1 is priced at that share and the rest are still phoned.
Input contract for s3: the damage report form in the app, filled by the driver; the paper accident statement with the other party is still filled in where required.
Phones and apps are used only when the van is stopped; accident calls and warnings keep their full time; the planner's time is outside the driver's savings.
s3 keeps 85 because only location, time and van fill in and the driver writes what happened; the photos, the check and the send keep their full time.
unknowns: How many delay calls a driver makes per day.
research_questions: Do planners still call drivers to ask where they are?

already_counted.description: Driver taps a delay reason when stopped for unusual delays.

incremental.description: Driver logs in and out of the app each shift.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: rural routes where most delays are unusual and still phoned in, so s1 keeps 75 (11.7); high: 70% of delays are routine and shown by the estimate (25.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
